title: Inhaler with a spacer for children
what: A spacer is a tube-shaped chamber between the inhaler and your child's mouth. The medicine goes into it first, and your child breathes it in calmly over a few breaths.
why: When your doctor prescribed a spray inhaler for your child, for asthma or wheezy bronchitis. It is hard for children to time a breath with the puff.
tell_doctor: How often your child needs the rescue inhaler
If your child cries and will not let you put on the mask
Ask the doctor to show you the technique at your visit

prepare.title: Mask or mouthpiece
prepare.text: Babies usually need a spacer with a mask. Older children use one with a mouthpiece. Your doctor will suggest which.

prepare.title: New spacer
prepare.text: Before first use, wash it in warm water with dish soap and let it air dry without wiping.

prepare.title: Mindset
prepare.text: Make it a game. It is easier if your child is calm.

bring: The inhaler and spacer, to your doctor's visit
steps: Take off the cap and shake the inhaler well
Put the inhaler into the spacer
Press the mask firmly on your child's face, covering the nose and mouth
Let your child take 5 to 6 calm breaths through the spacer
If a second dose is needed, shake again and repeat
After a steroid medicine, wipe your child's face and give a drink or a mouth rinse
feel: If your child cries, less medicine gets in. Try to calm them and repeat
after: Wash the spacer once a week, or as the leaflet says, and let it air dry
Take the spacer to kindergarten and on trips
red_flags: Your child breathes fast, the skin between the ribs pulls in, or it is hard to talk: call emergency services
Blue lips, or your child is very floppy: call emergency services

faq.q: Can I give two puffs at once?
faq.a: No. One puff, then the breaths. Then the next puff, if needed.

faq.q: If my child is crying, does the medicine get in?
faq.a: Not well. It is better to calm your child first. If that does not work, talk to your doctor.

reminders.text: Time for your child's inhaler. Shake, one puff into the spacer, then 5 to 6 calm breaths.
